original_question: What quantitative theoretical model can explain why, in SPS and similar hadron-collider observations, proton losses became more sensitive to high-order resonances when the opposing anti-proton bunch emittance was reduced to nearly match the proton emittance, even though the beam-beam parameter was about 40% lower?
target_in_paper: A quantitative theoretical model to explain these observations has not yet been developed.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the need for a quantitative theoretical model and captures the key observation that proton losses became more sensitive to high-order resonances when the anti-proton emittance was reduced to match the proton emittance despite a ~40% lower beam–beam parameter.
missing_details: Specific rms normalized emittance values of the proton (~5.5 π mm·mrad) and anti-proton (~7.5 π mm·mrad) bunches used in the SPS studies
The initial proton-to-anti-proton emittance ratio (≈4:1) and its reduction to ≈1:1
The order of the betatron resonances probed (13th and 16th order) and their role in proton losses
Definition of the per-interaction-point beam–beam tune shift parameter ξ
The head-on collision configuration (two collisions per turn) in the SPS
The failure of the existing scaling law (equation (3)) to predict the observed dependence
refined_question: In the CERN SPS proton–anti-proton collider, dedicated measurements in head-on collisions (two collisions per turn) showed that a proton bunch with rms normalized emittance ≈5.5 π mm·mrad was insensitive to the 13th and 16th order betatron resonances when colliding with an anti-proton bunch of ≈7.5 π mm·mrad (emittance ratio ≈4:1), but became highly sensitive to those same resonances after the anti-proton bunch was scraped to ≈5.5 π mm·mrad (emittance ratio ≈1:1), even though the per-interaction-point beam–beam tune shift parameter ξ was reduced by ≈40%. Existing scaling laws (e.g., equation (3) in the paper) fail to predict this behavior. What quantitative theoretical model can accurately reproduce and explain this enhanced proton loss sensitivity to the 13th and 16th order resonances under matched emittance conditions with reduced beam–beam parameter?
justification: Section 1.1.4.3 “Matching beam sizes” (page 12) of the paper describes the exact experimental observations—emittance values, resonance orders, collision configuration, and the ~40% reduction in the beam–beam tune shift parameter—and states that no quantitative theoretical model exists for these effects. The refined question restates this open problem with all necessary quantitative details and definitions, making it self-contained and faithful to the paper’s scope, whereas the draft omitted specific emittance values, resonance orders, collision details, and the failure of the existing scaling law.
